channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes State Visit to Oman, Signing Strategic Partnership Agreement
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has concluded his state visit to the Sultanate of Oman. During the visit, he held talks with Sultan Haitham bin Tarik and met with business leaders, resulting in a Strategic Partnership Agreement and over 30 other documents. A portfolio of projects worth $5 billion was formed.

item.title: Iran Reports US Strike on Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran has reported that the United States conducted a strike on facilities on the Iranian island of Qeshm on November 17. The deputy governor of Hormozgan province stated that residential, commercial, and infrastructure facilities were not affected. The nature of the targeted objects remains unspecified by Iranian authorities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Easing Visa Procedures with Canada
item.description: Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration head, Saida Mirziyoyeva, met with Canadian Ambassador Christopher Dagan to discuss expanding trade, investment, and educational cooperation, including easing visa procedures. Mirziyoyeva expressed confidence that joint initiatives will elevate mutual relations and create opportunities for citizens.

item.title: Pakistan Invites Turkmenistan to Join Central Asia-South Asia Electricity Project
item.description: Pakistan has invited Turkmenistan to join the CASA-1000 electricity transmission project, aiming to boost electricity trade between Central and South Asia. Pakistan's energy minister discussed the proposal with his Turkmen counterpart, also suggesting extending the transmission line to Uzbekistan. Pakistan seeks to address its energy shortages and develop its economy through these regional power projects.

item.title: New Compressor at Kazakhstan's Karachaganak Field to Maintain Production Levels
item.description: A sixth gas compressor has been commissioned at the Karachaganak field in Kazakhstan's West Kazakhstan region, capable of reinjecting up to 4 billion cubic meters of gas annually. This measure aims to maintain reservoir pressure and sustain oil production at 10-11 million tons per year. The project involved local employment and a significant share of Kazakhstani goods and services.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Test Self-Driving Vehicles on Astana Roads
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to test self-driving vehicles on designated routes in Astana as part of a three-year pilot project. The relevant draft decree is open for public discussion until December 2. Previously, driverless taxi services were planned for Astana, Almaty, and the Akmola region.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman to Triple Food Trade and Build New Fertilizer Plant
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman aim to triple food trade by 2027, focusing on exporting fruits, vegetables, and processed goods. They will also collaborate on agricultural projects, including a new $13 million liquid fertilizer and biological agents plant in Tashkent, creating up to 65 jobs.

item.title: Child Killed, Another Injured in Mortar Shell Explosion in Afghanistan's Ghazni Province
item.description: A child was killed and his younger brother seriously injured in a mortar shell explosion in Qala-e-Alam village, Deh Yak District, Ghazni province. This incident follows another child's death from an unexploded shell in Ghazni the previous day.

item.title: Central Asian Institute Discusses Jordanian King's Peace Initiatives
item.description: The International Institute of Central Asia (IICA) hosted a roundtable on "Seeking Peace in an Era of Instability," focusing on King Abdullah II of Jordan's ideas. Participants discussed Jordan's foreign policy, interfaith harmony, and countering extremism, as well as transport and economic cooperation prospects.

item.title: Two Representatives of Omid Sabz Township Remain in Taliban Custody
item.description: Two representatives of Omid Sabz Township in western Kabul have been in Taliban custody for nearly 10 days. Abdul Razeq Mosaddiq and Wakil Jafari were arrested after being summoned to the Taliban’s Ministry of Justice. Their families do not know their whereabouts.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Sign New Green Energy Cooperation Agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have signed a new agreement to develop green energy projects, including a 500 MW solar power station in the Fergana region. The agreement involves Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, and Omani company Voltamp Energy SAOG. The project aims to attract $350 million in foreign investment.

item.title: Taliban restrict women's access to healthcare by barring male doctors
item.description: The Taliban have ordered male doctors not to treat women, forcing patients like Farida to abandon medical treatment. This policy, despite claims of ensuring women see female doctors, restricts access to healthcare. It creates a precarious situation where women's treatment depends on the availability of female health workers, whose own education and work opportunities are being curtailed by the same authorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Rise in Internal Migration, Major Cities Attract Most Residents
item.description: Internal migration in Kazakhstan has increased, with a significant portion of the population moving to larger cities. Between January and September 2026, 1.4 million people changed their place of residence within the country, a 5.8% increase compared to the same period last year. Over the past decade, internal migration has more than tripled.

item.title: Debt of Rich Nations Impacts Poor Countries as Interest Rates Rise Post-Pandemic and War
item.description: The debt of wealthy nations is negatively affecting poorer countries, as central banks have raised interest rates following the pandemic and ongoing conflicts. This situation traps developing economies in financial difficulties, limiting their growth prospects. Currently, 51 countries spend more on debt interest payments than on public health and education.

item.title: UK Special Representative for Afghanistan Meets Taliban Ambassador in Pakistan
item.description: Richard Lindsay, the UK's Special Representative for Afghanistan, met with Sardar Ahmad Shakib, the Taliban's ambassador to Islamabad. They discussed bilateral relations, regional security, and the role of diplomatic dialogue in promoting stability. Lindsay had previously met with Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan to discuss regional peace.

item.title: Foreign Ministers of Oman, Iran, and Uzbekistan Discuss Regional Developments in Muscat
item.description: The foreign ministers of Oman, Iran, and Uzbekistan held talks in Muscat to discuss regional developments and de-escalation efforts. They emphasized resolving challenges through dialogue and respecting international law. The ministers also called for restoring freedom of navigation and ensuring safe international trade passage.

item.title: Russia's New Kamikaze Drone Capable of 1000 km/h Speeds
item.description: Russia has deployed a new kamikaze drone, the 'Geran-5 K5-K', equipped with a jet engine and capable of carrying a 90 kg warhead. This drone can strike targets up to 1000 km away and is considered by some experts to be a small cruise missile. Ukraine is developing countermeasures.

item.title: Ukraine Launches New Strikes on Crimean Bridge, Causing Damage
item.description: Ukrainian forces launched a second consecutive strike on the Crimean Bridge overnight, rendering the road section unusable. The railway section was also damaged. Ukrainian President Zelensky stated the operation was meticulously planned over weeks, involving the destruction of air defense systems and radars. Various drones and missiles were reportedly used.

item.title: Kazakh Language Must Become Language of Science and Innovation, Says Official
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin discussed improving language norms with experts to implement President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives. The initiative aims to systematize Kazakh language orthography and terminology, update dictionaries, and digitize vocabulary, fostering its future development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Puts Defense Enterprise 'Semey Engineering' Up for Sale
item.description: Kazakhstan Engineering National Company has put its 100% stake in the defense enterprise 'Semey Engineering' up for auction. The starting price is 70.8 billion tenge. The new owner must also assume the company's multi-billion tenge debt to the parent company.

item.title: Uzbek Official Meets with Canadian Ambassador to Discuss Bilateral Ties
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, met with the Canadian Ambassador. They focused on expanding trade, investment, business ties, educational cooperation, and simplifying visa procedures. Mirziyoyeva expressed confidence that joint initiatives will elevate relations and benefit citizens.

item.title: UN Allocates $18 Million in Emergency Aid for Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has approved $18 million in emergency aid for Afghanistan, set to benefit over 824,000 vulnerable individuals. Funding from the UN Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) will support seven projects in food security, agriculture, health, and other critical areas.

item.title: Jordan and Iraq to Ban Telegram Over Security and Content Concerns
item.description: Jordan and Iraq have announced plans to ban the messaging app Telegram, citing national security concerns. The measures aim to prevent the spread of illegal and extremist content and compel Telegram to review content related to the countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Saida Mirziyoyeva Discusses Visa Facilitation with Canadian Ambassador
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, met with Canada's Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Christopher Dagan. They discussed facilitating visa procedures and expanding trade, investment, and business ties between the two countries.

item.title: Five Uzbek Schoolchildren Involved in Fatal Car Crash, One Dies
item.description: Five eighth-grade students were involved in a car accident on a road outside a village in Toyloq district, Samarqand region. One student died from injuries sustained in the crash. The driver, also a student, reportedly hit a tree. An investigation is underway, and the incident highlights a prevalent issue of underage driving in Uzbekistan.

item.title: One-Year-Old Dies of Measles in Kazakhstan's Atyrau Region
item.description: A one-year-old child has died from measles in the Atyrau region of Kazakhstan. The child was airlifted to a regional infectious diseases hospital in critical condition, suffering from bilateral pneumonia and respiratory and cardiac failure. Doctors noted the child had a congenital heart defect and parents had refused vaccination.

item.title: Two Schoolboys Suspected of Abusing Child in Kazakhstan's Kostanay Region
item.description: In Kazakhstan's Kostanay region, two sixth-grade students are suspected of sexually abusing a 10-year-old boy in a school restroom. The police have opened a criminal case. The 'NeMolchiKZ' foundation reported the incident, stating the alleged perpetrators were 11 and 12 years old. The regional ombudsman for children's rights is monitoring the situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hosts Military Drone Challenge for State Agencies
item.description: A Military Drone Challenge tournament was held at the 'Maylan' field training center of the State Security Service of Kazakhstan. The competition aimed to improve skills in using and countering unmanned aerial systems. Teams from various Kazakh state bodies participated, with the State Security Service team securing first place.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Population Grew by Nearly 10 Million in 16 Years
item.description: Uzbekistan's permanent population has increased by almost 10 million people over the past 16 years. According to the Statistics Committee, the population grew from 29.2 million in early 2010 to 39 million by early 2026. The country surpassed 30 million residents in 2012 and has seen consistent demographic growth since.

item.title: Uzbekistan Leads CIS in Unemployment Rate Reduction Over Five Years
item.description: Uzbekistan has shown the most significant reduction in unemployment among CIS countries over the past five years, decreasing by over half from 10.5% in 2020 to 4.8% by the end of 2025. Kyrgyzstan also saw a notable decrease. Overall, unemployment in the CIS region fell from 3.4% to 3.1% between 2024 and 2025.

item.title: Kazakhstan Security Forces Compete in Drone Operations Challenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's security forces participated in the MILITARY DRONE CHALLENGE, a competition testing their skills in operating drones and countering unmanned aerial systems. Held at the 'Maylan' training ground, teams from various state bodies executed tasks simulating real-world scenarios. The State Security Service of Kazakhstan secured first place.

item.title: Astana Education Department Proposes ID Card for Class Attendance Tracking
item.description: The Astana Education Department suggests using ID cards for tracking student attendance in extracurricular activities if parents object to facial recognition. This aims to ensure budget funds are allocated correctly for attended classes. QR codes are also an option.

item.title: Oman's Voltamp Energy to Invest $350 Million in Uzbekistan Solar Power Plant
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have signed a joint development agreement for a 500 MW solar photovoltaic station in the Fergana region. Oman's Voltamp Energy SAOG will invest $350 million in the project. The plant is expected to generate 1 billion kWh of green electricity annually, saving 250 million cubic meters of natural gas.

item.title: Uzbekistan Holds Training on Practical Measures to Reduce Statelessness
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs participated in a training session in Tashkent focused on preventing and reducing statelessness. Organized by the National Human Rights Center and UNHCR, the event aimed to enhance officers' knowledge of international standards and practical skills in identifying and protecting stateless individuals.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Investment, Trade, and Transport with Eight European Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister held bilateral meetings with counterparts from Germany, Romania, Latvia, Estonia, Ukraine, France, Croatia, and Bulgaria. Discussions focused on economic development, enhancing transit-transport potential, and attracting European companies for infrastructure modernization. Particular attention was given to strengthening strategic partnership with Germany.

item.title: Kazakhstan Marks 35 Years of Independence and Economic Transformation
item.description: Kazakhstan celebrates 35 years of independence since December 16, 1991, highlighting significant economic growth and regional leadership. Despite initial post-Soviet challenges, reforms and foreign investment fueled expansion, particularly in the oil and gas sector. The nation has navigated global crises to become Central Asia's largest economy.

item.title: Taliban Envoy to Pakistan Discusses Regional Security with UK Representative
item.description: Sardar Ahmad Shakib, the Taliban envoy to Pakistan, met with Richard Lindsay, the UK's Special Representative for Afghanistan. They discussed Afghanistan-UK relations, regional security developments, and the importance of continued diplomatic engagement for stability. The Taliban envoy stated the meeting was constructive.

item.title: Guterres: Climate Crisis Accelerating, Urges Stepped-Up Protection Efforts
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated that extreme weather events are claiming lives and reversing development gains due to the accelerating climate crisis. He urged increased efforts to protect people, emphasizing preventive measures and timely information on natural hazards.

item.title: Deutsche Bank Documents Reveal Links to Trump, Epstein, and Russian Oligarchs
item.description: Over 15 million internal Deutsche Bank documents have been leaked, exposing connections to Russian oligarchs, Donald Trump, and Jeffrey Epstein. The bank may have processed $582 million in suspicious transactions related to Epstein and inadvertently disclosed Trump's tax documents. Bank shares fell over 6% following the leak.

item.title: The Economist Predicts 10 Key Global Trends for 2027
item.description: The Economist has identified 10 major trends shaping global politics, economy, and technology in 2027. Forecasts include increased pressure on global markets, rising military risks in certain regions, and record-breaking weather warming. These trends are expected to define the global landscape.
